modules.title: Analytics and Reporting
modules.goal: Turn transactional rows into cohorts, funnels, retention and time-series reports.

topics.title: Reporting SQL
topics.simple: Reporting queries business questions ko rows me badalte hain.
topics.pro: A reporting query defines the grain, filters the population, aggregates the measure and orders the result.

example.sql: SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS enrolled FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id ORDER BY enrolled DESC;

topics.title: Cohort Analysis
topics.simple: Cohort users ko shared start period me group karta hai.
topics.pro: A cohort groups entities by their first event period and tracks later behavior within each cohort.

example.sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', MIN(enrolled_on)) AS cohort, student_id FROM enrollments GROUP BY student_id;

topics.title: Funnel Analysis
topics.simple: Funnel steps ke conversions count karta hai.
topics.pro: A funnel counts how many entities reach each step, usually with conditional aggregation or self-joins.

example.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) FILTER (WHERE course_id = 10) AS step1 FROM enrollments;

topics.title: Retention
topics.simple: Retention wapas aane wale users count karta hai.
topics.pro: Retention compares a cohort’s later activity with its original size, often by period.

example.sql: SELECT student_id, COUNT(DISTINCT course_id) AS courses FROM enrollments GROUP BY student_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT course_id) > 1;
example.output: Students with more than one course.

topics.title: Time Series
topics.simple: Time series periods ke measures dikhata hai.
topics.pro: Time-series reports bucket dates with DATE_TRUNC and fill missing periods when the chart requires continuity.

example.sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', enrolled_on) AS month, COUNT(*) AS total FROM enrollments GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;

topics.title: Pivot with CASE
topics.simple: CASE se rows ko columns me pivot karo.
topics.pro: Conditional aggregation pivots categories into columns without a dedicated pivot operator.

example.sql: SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE enrolled_on >= DATE '2026-01-01') AS recent, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE enrolled_on < DATE '2026-01-01') AS older FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id;
example.output: Course rows with recent and older count columns.

topics.title: Crosstab
topics.simple: Crosstab rows aur columns ka matrix banata hai.
topics.pro: The tablefunc crosstab function turns long category rows into a wide matrix.

example.sql: SELECT * FROM crosstab('SELECT course_id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM enrolled_on)::int, COUNT(*) FROM enrollments GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2') AS ct(course_id int, y2025 bigint, y2026 bigint);

topics.title: Running Totals
topics.simple: Running totals cumulative progress dikhate hain.
topics.pro: A window SUM ordered by time produces cumulative totals for charts and targets.

example.sql: SELECT enrolled_on, COUNT(*) AS day_count, SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (ORDER BY enrolled_on) AS running FROM enrollments GROUP BY enrolled_on ORDER BY enrolled_on;

topics.title: Percent of Total
topics.simple: Percent of total share dikhata hai.
topics.pro: Divide the group measure by a window total to show each row’s share of the whole.

example.sql: SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS total, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id;

topics.title: Ranking
topics.simple: Ranking report ko ordered priority deta hai.
topics.pro: Window ranking orders groups by a measure while preserving every group row.

example.sql: SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS total, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id;

topics.title: Period Comparisons
topics.simple: Previous period se compare karo.
topics.pro: LAG or self-joins compare a period with the prior period, producing growth and deltas.

example.sql: SELECT month, total, total - LAG(total) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS delta FROM monthly_counts;

topics.title: Cohort Retention Table
topics.simple: Cohort ke har period ki retention calculate karo.
topics.pro: A cohort retention table joins each entity’s cohort month to later activity months and counts distinct returning entities.

example.sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', e.enrolled_on) AS activity_month, COUNT(DISTINCT e.student_id) AS active FROM enrollments e GROUP BY activity_month ORDER BY activity_month;

topics.title: Common Reporting Errors
topics.simple: Wrong grain, double counting aur timezone bugs common errors hain.
topics.pro: Common failures are joining one-to-many tables before aggregating, counting rows instead of entities, and mixing time zones.

example.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) FROM enrollments;

topics.title: Reporting Performance
topics.simple: Pre-aggregate aur index reporting queries.
topics.pro: Reports often scan large ranges; pre-aggregation, materialized views and date indexes reduce repeated work.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_enrollments_date ON enrollments (enrolled_on);

topics.title: Dashboard Queries
topics.simple: Dashboard ke liye fast, stable queries chahiye.
topics.pro: Dashboard queries should be bounded, indexed and cached where freshness allows.

example.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrollments WHERE enrolled_on >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days';

topics.title: Export Queries
topics.simple: Export ke liye deterministic ordering aur columns do.
topics.pro: Exports need stable column names, explicit ordering and no accidental row limits.

example.sql: SELECT student_id, course_id, enrolled_on FROM enrollments ORDER BY enrolled_on, student_id;

topics.title: Data Quality Checks
topics.simple: Reporting se pehle data quality check karo.
topics.pro: Checks catch NULLs, duplicates, orphan keys and impossible values before they distort a report.

example.sql: SELECT student_id, course_id, COUNT(*) FROM enrollments GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

topics.title: Timezone Reporting
topics.simple: Timestamps ko ek timezone me report karo.
topics.pro: TIMESTAMPTZ stores instants; convert to the reporting time zone before truncating dates.

example.sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', enrolled_on AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') AS day, COUNT(*) FROM enrollments GROUP BY day;

topics.title: Narrative Metrics
topics.simple: Metrics ke saath denominator aur definition do.
topics.pro: A trustworthy report states the denominator, the time window and the exact definition of each metric.

example.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE marks >= 60) AS passed, COUNT(*) AS total FROM students;
example.output: Passed and total with a clear denominator.

topics.title: Practical Dashboard
topics.simple: Cohort, funnel aur time series ko combine karo.
topics.pro: A practical dashboard query produces one row per period with counts, shares and comparisons, bounded to a recent window.

example.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', enrolled_on) AS month, COUNT(*) AS total FROM enrollments GROUP BY month) SELECT month, total, total - LAG(total) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS delta FROM monthly ORDER BY month;

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Reporting SQL in a production query.
interview.answer: A reporting query defines the grain, filters the population, aggregates the measure and orders the result. Key rules: State the grain. Define the population. Choose the measure.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Cohort Analysis in a production query.
interview.answer: A cohort groups entities by their first event period and tracks later behavior within each cohort. Key rules: Define the cohort date. Group by cohort. Measure later activity.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Funnel Analysis in a production query.
interview.answer: A funnel counts how many entities reach each step, usually with conditional aggregation or self-joins. Key rules: Define ordered steps. Count distinct entities. Compare step counts.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Retention in a production query.
interview.answer: Retention compares a cohort’s later activity with its original size, often by period. Key rules: Define active. Fix the cohort. Calculate the ratio.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Time Series in a production query.
interview.answer: Time-series reports bucket dates with DATE_TRUNC and fill missing periods when the chart requires continuity. Key rules: Bucket the date. Aggregate the measure. Fill gaps explicitly.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Pivot with CASE in a production query.
interview.answer: Conditional aggregation pivots categories into columns without a dedicated pivot operator. Key rules: One CASE per column. Aggregate each CASE. Group by the row key.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Crosstab in a production query.
interview.answer: The tablefunc crosstab function turns long category rows into a wide matrix. Key rules: Enable tablefunc. Define row and category columns. Name the output columns.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Running Totals in a production query.
interview.answer: A window SUM ordered by time produces cumulative totals for charts and targets. Key rules: Order by the period. Use an unbounded frame. Partition when needed.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Percent of Total in a production query.
interview.answer: Divide the group measure by a window total to show each row’s share of the whole. Key rules: Use SUM(...) OVER (). Guard zero. Round for display.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Ranking in a production query.
interview.answer: Window ranking orders groups by a measure while preserving every group row. Key rules: Rank by the measure. Break ties. Filter after ranking.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Period Comparisons in a production query.
interview.answer: LAG or self-joins compare a period with the prior period, producing growth and deltas. Key rules: Order periods. Use LAG. Handle missing periods.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Cohort Retention Table in a production query.
interview.answer: A cohort retention table joins each entity’s cohort month to later activity months and counts distinct returning entities. Key rules: Cohort month. Activity month. Count distinct entities. Divide by cohort size.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Common Reporting Errors in a production query.
interview.answer: Common failures are joining one-to-many tables before aggregating, counting rows instead of entities, and mixing time zones. Key rules: Check the grain. Count distinct entities. Normalize time zones.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Reporting Performance in a production query.
interview.answer: Reports often scan large ranges; pre-aggregation, materialized views and date indexes reduce repeated work. Key rules: Filter on dates. Pre-aggregate. Refresh materialized views.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Dashboard Queries in a production query.
interview.answer: Dashboard queries should be bounded, indexed and cached where freshness allows. Key rules: Bound the date range. Limit rows. Cache or materialize.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Export Queries in a production query.
interview.answer: Exports need stable column names, explicit ordering and no accidental row limits. Key rules: Order explicitly. Select explicit columns. Avoid SELECT *.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Data Quality Checks in a production query.
interview.answer: Checks catch NULLs, duplicates, orphan keys and impossible values before they distort a report. Key rules: Check duplicates. Check orphans. Check ranges.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Timezone Reporting in a production query.
interview.answer: TIMESTAMPTZ stores instants; convert to the reporting time zone before truncating dates. Key rules: Store timestamptz. Convert at the boundary. Document the zone.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Narrative Metrics in a production query.
interview.answer: A trustworthy report states the denominator, the time window and the exact definition of each metric. Key rules: Define the metric. Show the denominator. State the window.

interview.q: Module 34 · Explain Practical Dashboard in a production query.
interview.answer: A practical dashboard query produces one row per period with counts, shares and comparisons, bounded to a recent window. Key rules: Bound the window. Use CTEs. Keep the grain explicit.

debug.title: Double counting
debug.broken: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id;
debug.fix: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id;
debug.error: One student with three enrollments counts three times

debug.title: Wrong grain
debug.broken: SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) FROM enrollments JOIN students ON students.id = enrollments.student_id;
debug.fix: SELECT course_id, COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id;
debug.error: The join changes the row grain

debug.title: Missing date bound
debug.fix: SELECT * FROM enrollments WHERE enrolled_on >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days';
debug.error: The report scans the full history

debug.title: Timezone mix
debug.fix: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', enrolled_on AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') FROM enrollments;
debug.error: Days are bucketed in the session zone

debug.title: Pivot without aggregate
debug.broken: SELECT course_id, CASE WHEN enrolled_on >= DATE '2026-01-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END FROM enrollments;
debug.fix: SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE enrolled_on >= DATE '2026-01-01') AS recent FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id;

debug.title: Funnel counts rows
debug.broken: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrollments WHERE course_id = 10;
debug.fix: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) FROM enrollments WHERE course_id = 10;
debug.error: A student can appear multiple times

debug.title: LAG missing order
debug.broken: SELECT total, LAG(total) OVER () FROM monthly_counts;
debug.fix: SELECT total, LAG(total) OVER (ORDER BY month) FROM monthly_counts;

debug.title: Percent of zero
debug.broken: SELECT 100 * total / SUM(total) OVER () FROM monthly_counts;
debug.fix: SELECT 100.0 * total / NULLIF(SUM(total) OVER (), 0) FROM monthly_counts;
debug.error: division by zero when the total is zero

debug.title: Cohort wrong key
debug.broken: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', enrolled_on) AS cohort, COUNT(*) FROM enrollments GROUP BY cohort;
debug.fix: Group by the student first-enrollment month, then track later activity.
debug.error: The cohort is the activity month, not the first month

debug.title: Report without order
debug.broken: SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id;
debug.fix: SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id ORDER BY course_id;
debug.error: The export order is not guaranteed
